# J2a — Oracle panel: does exact committee force UQ predict reference-force error?

**Status:** complete. Every number below is generated by
`experiments/j2a_oracle_panel.py` from `results/records/j2a_oracle_panel.jsonl`
(136 records) and none was transcribed by hand.

**Method.** Six committed float64 head-force caches (3BPA@1200 K × three committee
constructions; rMD17 ethanol/aspirin/azobenzene). Reference error is
`Δ = mean_m F_m − F_DFT`, reduced four ways; uncertainty is the unbiased
over-head variance reduced by the three acquisition scalars the paper defines.
**Nothing is fitted** — no basis, no conformal constant, no threshold — so there
is no leakage risk and the full evaluation set is used. To be re-run on the J1
test split once split manifests exist, as a confirmation.

Runtime: **5.4 s on CPU.** No GPU, no model execution, no data download.

---

## 1. Factor A — the oracle is *moderate*, not strong and not worthless

AUROC for detecting the top-5% highest-`e_max` structures:

| system | exact global | exact max-comp | exact max-atom | energy std (free) | ‖f̄‖ (free) | random |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3BPA disjoint | **0.773** | 0.708 | 0.709 | 0.632 | 0.637 | 0.516 |
| 3BPA overlapping | **0.788** | 0.772 | 0.772 | — | 0.606 | 0.492 |
| 3BPA same | **0.848** | 0.824 | 0.838 | — | 0.702 | 0.495 |
| rMD17 ethanol | **0.737** | 0.691 | 0.662 | 0.650 | 0.670 | 0.469 |
| rMD17 aspirin | **0.760** | 0.653 | 0.696 | 0.667 | 0.647 | 0.530 |
| rMD17 azobenzene | **0.830** | 0.759 | 0.723 | 0.662 | 0.600 | 0.483 |

The random null sits at 0.469–0.530 across all six systems, which is the
sanity check that the metric implementation is sound (it is also verified against
brute-force all-pairs AUROC in float64, against tie-averaged ranks, and against a
hand-computed average-precision example).

### With block-bootstrap intervals

Added after J1's autocorrelation machinery landed. Block length is
`ceil(2·τ_int)` from the measured integrated autocorrelation time of each error
series; **100,000 resamples**, paired over structures, seed recorded in the
record's `meta` block. Regenerated by `experiments/j2a_confidence_intervals.py`
— see the correction note in §3 for why.

| system | exact global AUROC | 95% CI (block) |
|---|---|---|
| 3BPA disjoint | 0.773 | [0.729, 0.814] |
| 3BPA overlapping | 0.788 | [0.746, 0.827] |
| 3BPA same | 0.848 | [0.815, 0.877] |
| rMD17 ethanol | 0.737 | [0.657, 0.812] |
| rMD17 aspirin | 0.760 | [0.702, 0.814] |
| rMD17 azobenzene | 0.830 | [0.779, 0.877] |

### Regime call — and it depends on which statistic is primary

The pre-registered decision rule was **R-A iff AUROC(3BPA) ≥ 0.75 and ≥ 0.70 on
at least two rMD17 molecules**. The answer differs by statistic, which is itself
the finding:

- **Under max-component** (the rule Beck et al. used, and the workshop's primary):
  3BPA 0.708, ethanol 0.691, aspirin 0.653 — **regime R-B**.
- **Under the global statistic**: 3BPA 0.773, and *all three* rMD17 molecules at
  0.737–0.830 — **regime R-A**, on point estimates.

So switching to the statistic that a pre-registered comparison independently
identified as better (§2) also moves the project from a scoped claim to the full
application claim. Two honesty caveats: 3BPA disjoint's lower CI bound (0.729)
sits just under the 0.75 threshold, so R-A is met on point estimates rather than
uniformly on intervals; and the switch must be reported as what it is — a
pre-registered secondary hypothesis that came out 24/24, not a post-hoc choice.

## 2. The decisive finding — the global statistic wins, unanimously

The pre-registered high-upside hypothesis was that the *easier-to-sketch* global
statistic might also be the *better physical predictor*. It is, in **24 of 24**
(system × error-score) cells:

| system | e_max | e_maxcomp | e_rmse | e_q95 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3BPA disjoint | +0.065 | +0.064 | +0.115 | +0.117 |
| 3BPA overlapping | +0.016 | +0.020 | +0.045 | +0.059 |
| 3BPA same | +0.024 | +0.018 | +0.061 | +0.077 |
| rMD17 ethanol | +0.046 | +0.103 | +0.086 | +0.075 |
| rMD17 aspirin | +0.106 | +0.073 | +0.116 | +0.075 |
| rMD17 azobenzene | +0.071 | +0.053 | +0.063 | +0.064 |

(AUROC advantage of `exact_global` over `exact_maxcomp`.) It is not a
reduction artifact: the advantage holds when the error score is matched to the
signal's own reduction (`e_maxcomp`) just as it does for atom-max and RMS errors.
On Spearman the margin is larger still — e.g. 0.479 vs 0.337 on 3BPA disjoint,
0.368 vs 0.248 on aspirin.

**With paired block-bootstrap intervals: 24/24 positive, 19/24 significant at
95%, and not one cell significantly negative.** The five non-significant cells
are all small positive deltas (+0.016 to +0.046) on the two low-diversity 3BPA
committees and on ethanol's `e_max`. The defensible sentence is therefore *"the
global statistic is never worse and is significantly better in 19 of 24
comparisons"*, not a bare 24/24. Full intervals in
`results/records/j2a_global_vs_maxcomp_ci.json`.

**Why this matters more than any other number in the project.** The workshop
paper's headline negative result is that the *max-component* rule cannot be
sketched at small K (recall 0.484–0.570 at K=4). The global statistic is
*statistically easier* to sketch — it concentrates over 3N coordinates, and its
K=4 recall is already 0.619 (0.730 with the control variate). We now know it is
**also the better predictor of physical error**. The negative result therefore
applies to the statistic one should not have been using, and the recommendation
becomes constructive rather than cautionary.

## 3. Force UQ does buy something over free signals — quantifiably

Head-energy spread costs one forward pass; mean-force magnitude is already
computed. Both are genuinely informative (0.60–0.70), which is itself worth
reporting. But the exact global force disagreement beats the better of them by:

| system | best free | exact global | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 3BPA disjoint | 0.637 | 0.773 | **+0.136** |
| 3BPA overlapping | 0.606 | 0.788 | **+0.182** |
| 3BPA same | 0.702 | 0.848 | **+0.146** |
| rMD17 ethanol | 0.670 | 0.737 | +0.067 |
| rMD17 aspirin | 0.667 | 0.760 | +0.093 |
| rMD17 azobenzene | 0.662 | 0.830 | **+0.169** |

With paired block-bootstrap intervals the *pairwise* advantage (against each free
signal separately) is **significant in 9 of 10** comparisons and spans +0.067 to
+0.230; the gain over the **best** free signal per system — the quantity in the
table above — is smaller, **+0.067 to +0.182**. The single exception is
`force_norm` on ethanol (+0.067, CI [−0.030, +0.165]), positive but not resolved
at n=1000.

> **Corrected, and the reason matters more than the number.** This said "8 of 10"
> and listed aspirin's `force_norm` (+0.112) as a second exception. Both CI records
> behind this section turned out to have **no generating script and no recorded
> seed** — they were produced by an ad-hoc computation in an earlier session and
> could not be regenerated, which is precisely the hole R1/R3 exist to close. They
> are now produced by `experiments/j2a_confidence_intervals.py` at 100,000
> resamples with the seed recorded, and the old copies are kept under
> `results/records/superseded/`. **The headline is unchanged — still 24/24
> positive and 19/24 significant** — but aspirin's `force_norm` interval resolves
> above zero (+0.112, CI [+0.008, +0.216]), making it 9 of 10. The lesson is that
> an unreproducible record can be wrong in either direction; this one happened to
> understate the result.

So the backward passes are worth paying for — by a margin that is real but not
overwhelming, which is precisely the kind of honest scoping a methods referee
wants and which no prior work on multi-head committees has reported.

Selective-risk excess area (0 = oracle, 1 = worthless) tells the same story with
the same ordering: global 0.36–0.60, max-component 0.45–0.72, energy 0.69–0.80.

## 4. An unexpected mechanism: committee diversity is *inversely* related to error detection

The three 3BPA committees differ only in how training data was split across heads,
and their disagreement magnitudes differ by 4.6× (median atom disagreement 33.5 /
12.8 / 7.2 meV/Å for disjoint / overlapping / same, per `checkpoints.json`). Error
detection runs the *opposite* way:

| committee | median atom disagreement | AUROC (global, e_max) |
|---|---|---|
| disjoint | 33.5 meV/Å | 0.773 |
| overlapping | 12.8 meV/Å | 0.788 |
| same | 7.2 meV/Å | **0.848** |

The least diverse committee — the one whose heads saw identical data and differ
only by initialisation, and which is therefore the *most* overconfident in
magnitude (7.2 meV/Å against a ~191 meV/Å force RMSE, ~26× off) — ranks
reference error the *best*. Magnitude calibration and rank informativeness are
different properties, and optimising a committee for spread does not optimise it
for acquisition. This axis is free (all three caches are committed), was not in
the plan, and is a candidate mechanism section.

---

## Consequences for the programme

1. **Promote the global statistic to primary**, with the max-component rule
   retained as the rule Beck et al. actually used and the one the negative result
   is about. This is a change of recommendation, not a change of scope.

   > **Scoped by J6B — this now carries a fixed-N condition.** On 136,923 MPtraj
   > crystals of 1–444 atoms the global statistic loses to max-component on all
   > four error scores, every one significant (−0.023 to −0.045). The mechanism is
   > extensivity: the global statistic sums `v_d` over 3N coordinates, so it grows
   > with system size regardless of uncertainty, and acquiring by it returns a
   > median of 70 atoms from a pool whose median is 20 (correlation with N: 0.631
   > against max-component's 0.285). Every system in this panel has **fixed N**,
   > where an extensive and an intensive statistic differ by a constant and the
   > pathology cannot appear. The 24/24 result stands as measured; the
   > recommendation must read *"at fixed system size"*, and ranking structures of
   > differing size needs a normalisation (dividing by 3N is the obvious
   > candidate and is untested). See `J6B_FOUNDATION_ACQUISITION.md`.
2. **Factor B (J2 full) is now worth running**, and should be evaluated primarily
   on the global statistic where the control variate already reaches 0.730 recall
   at K=4.
3. **Regime R-B framing**: add the "when is committee force UQ worth computing?"
   scoping section, carrying the free-signal comparison in §3.
4. **Venue: JCTC**, as planned. Factor A is comfortably above the R-C threshold
   that would have forced a restructure toward MLST.
5. The committee-diversity inversion in §4 needs a mechanism before it is claimed;
   the residual-spectrum analysis (J3.4) is the natural instrument.

## Caveats that must survive

- `E` (head energies) is **absent** from the `overlapping` and `same` caches, so
  the free `energy_std` baseline is missing for two of six systems. Regenerating
  those two caches is ~2 GPU-minutes once `fs-gpu` exists.
- Computed on the full evaluation set. Legitimate here because nothing is fitted,
  but it must be re-run on the J1 test split for the record.
- Single-frame ("instantaneous") force error. A committee that ranks *trajectory*
  reliability well could score modestly here; that is a limitation of the metric,
  not necessarily of the committee.
- ~~Confidence intervals are not yet attached~~ **— they now are**, in §1 and §2
  above (block bootstrap, 10,000 resamples). The 24/24 count became "24/24
  positive, 19/24 significant" once they were.

## Provenance defect found while validating the caches

`utils/reproducibility.py:73` `checkpoint_param_sha256` documents itself as
dtype-invariant ("an fp32 checkpoint and its fp64 copy share a hash") but hashes
`str(t.dtype)` alongside the float64-cast bytes, so it is not. Consequence:
`00_validate_checkpoints.py:96` loads at float32 and `01_exact_reproduction.py:96`
at float64, so **no cache's `checkpoint_hash` matches `checkpoints.json`** —
98e44023749c vs 71ab2b8b07cc for 3BPA disjoint, and so on. The same checkpoint
files were used; only the provenance label differs, so no science is affected.
But the hash cannot currently verify that a cache came from the manifest's
checkpoint, which is a real hole in the R1 chain. One-line fix (drop the dtype
update) in the journal package, as a new function — the frozen tree is not edited.
